description: Create Playwright end-to-end tests covering the full multi-user flow: registration, login, key management, usage tracking, and quota enforcement. Tests run against the actual dev server with MULTI_USER_MODE=true.
steps: Step 1: Install Playwright as a dev dependency in the project root: npm install -D @playwright/test. Create playwright.config.js at project root with baseURL http://localhost:20128, webServer config to start the dev server with MULTI_USER_MODE=true DATA_DIR=./test-data.

Step 2: Create tests/e2e/multi-user/registration.spec.js - Test user registration flow: POST /api/multi/register with valid data returns 201 + token; duplicate username returns 409; invalid password returns 400; when MULTI_USER_REGISTRATION=false returns 403.
Step 3: Create tests/e2e/multi-user/login.spec.js - Test login flow: POST /api/multi/login with valid credentials returns token; wrong password returns 401; non-existent user returns 401.

Step 4: Create tests/e2e/multi-user/keys.spec.js - Test key management: create key (POST /api/multi/keys), list keys (GET /api/multi/keys), delete key (DELETE /api/multi/keys?id=xxx). Verify max keys limit. Verify unauthorized access returns 401.
Step 5: Create tests/e2e/multi-user/usage.spec.js - Test usage endpoint: GET /api/multi/usage returns usage data for the user's keys. Verify filtering by period works.

Step 6: Create tests/e2e/multi-user/quota.spec.js - Test quota enforcement: set a very low quota for a test user, make requests that exceed the quota, verify 429 is returned with quota exceeded message.
Step 7: Create tests/e2e/multi-user/admin.spec.js - Test admin endpoints: create an admin user, verify they can list/update/delete other users. Verify non-admin users get 403.

Step 8: Create tests/e2e/multi-user/ui-flow.spec.js - Playwright browser tests for the user portal UI: navigate to /user-portal/register, fill form, submit, verify redirect to dashboard. Navigate to keys page, create a key, verify it appears. Navigate to usage page, verify it loads.
Step 9: Add npm script to package.json: 'test:e2e': 'npx playwright test tests/e2e/' and 'test:e2e:multi': 'npx playwright test tests/e2e/multi-user/'
Step 10: Run the Playwright tests and fix any issues that arise. Ensure all tests pass.
acceptance_criteria: All e2e test files are created covering registration, login, keys, usage, quota, admin, and UI flows
Tests can be run with `npx playwright test tests/e2e/multi-user/`
All tests pass against the running dev server with MULTI_USER_MODE=true
verification: MULTI_USER_MODE=true DATA_DIR=./test-data npx playwright test tests/e2e/multi-user/ passes all tests
npm run build still succeeds after test changes
findings: 1. DATA_DIR must be set to an absolute path outside the project directory (e.g., /tmp/9router-test-data) to avoid Next.js dev server hot-reload issues (Manifest file is empty error). 2. The first registered user does NOT automatically become admin - the codebase sets all users to role='user'. Admin tests use better-sqlite3 to directly promote a user in the SQLite DB at DATA_DIR/db/data.sqlite. 3. Chromium requires system libraries (nss, libxkbcommon, atk, cups-libs, etc.) - run npx playwright install-deps or install manually on Amazon Linux. 4. The webServer config uses reuseExistingServer to avoid startup delays on repeated local runs. 5. All 36 tests pass consistently: 7 admin, 6 keys, 4 login, 3 quota, 6 registration, 6 UI flow, 4 usage.
